title: The Pulse, Monday 5 October 2026
tldr: Aleph Alpha released Kolibri, a sovereign open-weight German LLM with real traction on HN. Claude Code added the "You Should Know" plugin to catch important output you might miss. DuplexJev proposes batched speech decisions without decoding — 80 decisions per second on an 8-GPU node, directly useful for full-duplex voice agents.

models.title: inclusionAI: Ling 3.1 Flash
models.summary: A hybrid reasoning mixture-of-experts model with 25B active parameters out of 560B total, now on OpenRouter.
models.why: Worth knowing, no direct use for us yet.

models.title: Google DiarizationLM-Gemma-4-E4B-v1
models.summary: A Gemma-4 based speaker diarization model released on Hugging Face.
models.why: EverRaise's voice agents on Vapi need accurate speaker identification in multi-party calls.

research.title: Batched Speech Decisions Without Decoding: Single-Token Supervision Lets a Frozen LLM Hear Beyond the Transcript
research.summary: DuplexJev feeds ASR-encoder hidden states through a small connector into a frozen LLM and reads each question as a single-token distribution over options, answering 80 decisions per second on an 8-GPU node without any decoding.
research.why: EverRaise's full-duplex voice agents make many small real-time decisions; this approach could drastically cut latency.

research.title: OpenGameEval: Benchmarking Agentic Programming and Exploration in a Stateful Game Engine
research.summary: A benchmark that turns Roblox Studio into an executable planning environment with reproducible, stateful game-engine sessions and executable checks.
research.why: Relevant benchmark structure for our own agentic code evaluation work and wehshi review panels.

research.title: Trained Agentic Context Management
research.summary: Fine-tunes Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with tools to call itself with any prompt and read tokens from input context in a range, treating context management as an agentic skill rather than a native model capability.
research.why: Hermes's context management for long tasks could benefit from this approach rather than packing everything into one window.

research.title: APDMem: Agent-Controlled Progressive Disclosure for Query-Adaptive Long-Term Memory
research.summary: A hierarchical long-term memory architecture that applies progressive disclosure to memory retrieval, adapting to query complexity rather than using flat Top-K.
research.why: Botterfly's Mnemosyne memory system could benefit from hierarchical retrieval rather than always returning fixed-count results.

releases.title: Python 3.15.0rc3
releases.summary: Release candidate 3 for Python 3.15.0, published October 2.
releases.why: Every Python interpreter release matters for our services; we test release candidates before production upgrades.

releases.title: langchain-text-splitters 1.1.3
releases.summary: Dependency updates including tornado, urllib3, anyio, soupsieve, and lxml.
releases.why: EverRaise and Mackinac both use LangChain for retrieval pipelines; dependency updates sometimes fix memory leaks or security issues.

releases.title: Langfuse v4.50.0
releases.summary: Adds facet type evaluators, built-in protection, rule idle time, seven-day execution health in evaluator status, and various fixes.
releases.why: We use Langfuse for observability across SalesKick and Pipeline clients; evaluator health monitoring is directly useful.

hackernews.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign Open-Weight Model
hackernews.summary: Aleph Alpha released Kolibri, an open-weight German LLM with 659 points and 326 comments on HN.
hackernews.why: Worth knowing; no direct use yet, but sovereign models show how regional players are competing outside the big three.

hackernews.title: Run Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (125B) on consumer hardware (RTX 4090) at 100T/s
hackernews.summary: A project demonstrating 125B parameter model inference at 100 tokens per second on a single RTX 4090.
hackernews.why: On-premises inference for clients with data residency requirements; shows what's now feasible on consumer hardware.

hackernews.title: We're going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything
hackernews.summary: Simon Willison argues for default hard spend limits on API services to prevent runaway costs from agentic systems.
hackernews.why: SalesKick's agentic flows and EverRaise's voice agents could rack up unexpected bills; budget caps deserve a place in our deployment checklist.

hackernews.title: Getting the most out of Opus 5.5 in Claude and Claude Code
hackernews.summary: Official guide on using Opus 5.5, with 232 points and 157 comments.
hackernews.why: Our team uses Claude Code daily; knowing how to get the best results from Opus 5.5 improves everyone's coding speed.

hackernews.title: Agents don't need memory, they need documentation
hackernews.summary: A post arguing structured documentation beats memory for agent context, with 354 points and 238 comments.
hackernews.why: Challenges our investment in Mnemosyne; the counter-argument is worth reading and the HN thread has smart takes on when each approach wins.

x_posts.title: Claude Code's "You Should Know" plugin
x_posts.summary: ClaudeDevs announced a new plugin that scans Claude's output for important information you might miss, enabled with /plugin enable cc-plugin-you-should-know@builtin.
x_posts.why: We use Claude Code on every project; this plugin helps catch decisions and warnings we'd otherwise scroll past.

x_posts.title: Linus Tech Tips discusses Hermes Agent
x_posts.summary: Nous Research noted that Linus Sebastian discussed his Hermes setup experience on their latest podcast.
x_posts.why: Hermes is our agent runtime; seeing it reach mainstream tech creators means support and plugin ecosystems will grow.

x_posts.title: Sebastian Raschka: Reasoning from Scratch, Round 6
x_posts.summary: An introduction and implementation of RLVR and GRPO for reasoning models.
x_posts.why: Reasoning traces underpin our code review workflows; GRPO is worth understanding if we ever fine-tune a reasoning model ourselves.
